title: Stop a retry lineage after 3 failed attempts and queue a narrower
summary: Add a documented default: when a retry lineage reaches 3 rejected or failed attempts, Athena dispatches no 4th attempt, records the repeated findings, and queues one narrower re-scope/split request instead. Goal: the maintainer no longer stops or splits runaway lineages by hand; the audience is the maintainer and the verifier, who check a test showing the 4th attempt is not dispatched.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus fmt, clippy and test pass.
The limit is enforced in drain code, not prose.
Tests exercise the 4th attempt not being dispatched.
Docs and changelog explain the limit.
One focused change to retry counting, drain and a default.
Caps the lineage, not the single instance.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/reading/retry.rs (earlier_attempt, retries_by_job, job_history, retried_job) and the crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs module doc and Steps/RunStep types; the drain today gives each item two attempts and a retry is a new job linked by 'try again on <job>'. The new cap counts rejected or failed jobs along that chain, so it is measured directly on job records, not through a stand-in. No new record file is added under crates/, so check_record_file/AnyRecord are untouched.
Existing code: extends crates/athena-core/src/reading/retry.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs and defaults.toml; reuses the finding text from retry_findings in retry.rs.
The cited intervention record is not readable here; I take its stated facts from the request: lineages ran 3 to 5 rejected attempts before manual stop or split.
The limit applies across manual and drain retries of one lineage; 'attempt' means a job ending rejected or failed.
The replacement request is queued through the drain's existing request queue, once per lineage (no duplicates on later passes).
Term lineage: a chain of jobs where each is a retry of the previous one.

acceptance_criteria.text: defaults.toml has a new entry (own id, statement, source naming records/interventions/2026-10/20261026-180231-tf2p.json) stating: at 3 rejected or failed attempts in one retry lineage, Athena stops retrying, records the repeated findings and queues one narrower re-scope or split request; and states whether it is enforced by mechanism.

A lineage-length helper in crates/athena-core/src/reading/retry.rs (built on the existing retries_by_job/job_history chain) counts the rejected or failed attempts in a lineage, and the limit 3 is a named constant or config value, visible in the diff.
A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (or retry.rs) builds a lineage with 3 rejected attempts and shows the drain starts no 4th attempt; run `cargo test` and the named test passes.

The same or a sibling test shows exactly one narrower re-scope/split request is queued in place of the retry, and that its text carries the findings that repeated across the attempts; run `cargo test`.

docs (docs/design/async-drain.md or the retry section of the drain module doc in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs) documents the 3-attempt lineage limit and the replacement request; CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
Lineages with fewer than 3 failed attempts behave as before: the existing tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs and drain.rs pass unchanged; run `cargo test`.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo test` all pass.
The diff changes no file under records/ and no governance file other than defaults.toml.

out_of_scope: Changing the two-attempt per-item rule inside a single drain run
Editing records/ or the intervention record itself
Changing the thrash-stop default text beyond cross-referencing
departures: Hard drain change touching retry flow across crates; costlier and less likely to pass than the reference.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time from lineages that ran 3 to 5 rejected attempts before a person stopped them by hand.
hard_reason: Adds a limit that holds work in the drain and changes the run pipeline's retry behavior, so a mistake is costly and hard to see.
